chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who had a wife who had become pure from her menstruation, so he went to a group and said, 'So-and-so woman is divorced.' Does the divorce occur upon her, and he did not say to them, 'Bear witness'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: Does a divorce count if the husband doesn't tell the witnesses to 'bear witness'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the explicit verbal command 'bear witness' is not a strict condition for the validity of talaq, as the Imam confirms the divorce is effective when declared in the presence of witnesses. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the substantive presence of witnesses over rigid formalistic formulas, distinguishing it from schools that may require specific phrasing. It underscores the practical flexibility in marital jurisprudence while maintaining the requirement of witness awareness.
